chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn 'Uthafir, from 'Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When it is the Day of Tarwiyah, do as you did with the tree, then pray two rak'ahs behind the Maqam (Station of Abraham), then announce the Ihram for Hajj. If you are walking, announce the Talbiyah at the Maqam; and if you are riding, [announce it] when your camel stands up for you. And pray the Dhuhr prayer if you are able in Mina. And know that it is permissible for you to enter the state of Ihram after every obligatory prayer, or after every voluntary prayer, or at night, or during the day."
And whoever makes a mistake and enters the state of Ihram for 'Umrah while intending Hajj, he should proceed with the Hajj, and there is no penalty upon him.

key_terms.أَهَلَّ بِالْحَجِّ: To announce the Ihram for Hajj
key_terms.الشَّجَرَةِ: The Tree (referring to the specific ritual action performed by the Prophet or Imam at this location)
key_terms.الْمَقَامُ: The Maqam (Station of Abraham near the Kaaba)
key_terms.لَبِّ: To announce the Talbiyah (the ritual invocation)

ai.seo_question: What are the correct procedures for entering Ihram on the Day of Tarwiyah and what is the ruling if one mistakes the intention?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) details the specific rites for the Day of Tarwiyah, emphasizing the flexibility of entering Ihram after any obligatory or voluntary prayer, a ruling that underscores the ease (taysir) in Shia jurisprudence. The narration also clarifies the legal principle of 'continuation of intention' (istishab al-niyya), ensuring that a mistake in declaring 'Umrah does not invalidate the Hajj if the primary intent was preserved.
